explanation_en: Part 4 says what a person achieves should be the result of hard work and talents, and that class distinctions should not limit anyone.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: In Australia, individuals must respect
options_en: only those people who share their own views and opinions.
the freedom, dignity, opinions and choices of others.
only people from the same background.
explanation_en: Part 4 says individuals must respect the freedom and dignity of others, and their opinions and choices.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A man screams abuse at a shop worker and threatens her. In Australia, verbal abuse like this is
options_en: legal as long as he does not touch her.
legal if he was provoked by poor service.
illegal, just like physical violence.
explanation_en: The booklet says violence of any kind, including verbal and physical abuse, is illegal in Australia.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Australians believe in
options_en: settling disagreements by force whenever words have failed.
peaceful disagreement and the right to be safe from violence.
avoiding disagreement by never discussing differences with anyone.
explanation_en: Part 4 says Australians believe in peaceful disagreement and above all the right to be safe and free from violence and intimidation.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: The age of sexual consent in Australia is
options_en: 16 or 17, depending on the state or territory.
14 years in every Australian state and territory.
21 in every state and territory.
explanation_en: The booklet says there are very strict laws on the age of sexual consent, which is 16 or 17 depending on which state or territory you live in.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A 20-year-old wants a sexual relationship with a 15-year-old. In Australia this is
options_en: legal in some states and territories but not others.
against the law in every state and territory.
legal if both of them agree.
explanation_en: Part 4 gives this exact example: a 20-year-old cannot have sexual relations with a 15-year-old because it is against the law in all Australian states and territories.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A police officer lawfully asks you to move away from an area. What should you do?
options_en: Obey the lawful request.
Ignore it unless you agree.
Argue until the officer gives up.
explanation_en: The booklet says the lawful actions of the police should be supported and you should obey a lawful request from the police.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Which behaviour shows the Australian value of mutual respect and tolerance?
options_en: Listening only to people who already agree with your own views.
Listening to others and respecting their views, even when they differ from yours.
Staying silent on every controversial topic to avoid any argument.
explanation_en: Part 4 says mutual respect and tolerance means listening to others and respecting their views and opinions, even when they differ from your own.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: At a football match, a spectator shouts racial abuse at a player. In Australia this is
options_en: racism, which has no place in Australia.
a normal part of the game.
acceptable if the home team is losing the match.
explanation_en: The booklet says racism has no place in Australia, including racially abusive comments in a public place or at a sporting event.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A friend shares a racially offensive image in an online group. In Australia this is
options_en: not acceptable; racism has no place in Australia.
fine, because it is only online.
fine, because it is only shared among close friends.
explanation_en: Part 4 says racism has no place in Australia, including creating or sharing racially offensive material on the internet.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Two neighbours strongly disagree about politics. Which behaviour reflects Australian values?
options_en: Discussing it peacefully and tolerating each other.
Threatening each other until one gives in.
Reporting each other to the police for disagreeing.
explanation_en: The booklet says people should be tolerant of each other where they disagree and believes in peaceful disagreement.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Racism includes
options_en: prejudice or hatred towards someone because of their race.
disagreeing strongly with someone about politics or religion.
supporting a different sporting team.
explanation_en: The glossary defines racism as prejudice, discrimination, harassment or hatred directed at someone because of their race, colour, national or ethnic origin.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: In Australia, where can racism be reported?
options_en: The Governor-General's office.
The Australian Electoral Commission or a local council.
The police or the Australian Human Rights Commission.
explanation_en: The glossary says racism is against the law and can be reported to the police or the Australian Human Rights Commission.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: What does the Australian Human Rights Commission do?
options_en: Decides the penalties handed down to offenders in criminal trials.
Looks into complaints of discrimination and human rights breaches.
Runs federal elections and counts the votes.
explanation_en: The glossary describes the Australian Human Rights Commission as an independent commission that investigates complaints about discrimination and human rights breaches.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: Your neighbour insults your car. Is it acceptable to push him?
options_en: Yes, if he insulted you first.
No; violence of any kind is illegal.
Yes, as long as he is not seriously injured.
explanation_en: Part 4 says it is against the law to be violent towards another person; violence of any kind is illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Australian values are central to the community remaining
options_en: secure, prosperous and peaceful.
closed to people from other cultures.
divided by wealth and social class.
explanation_en: Part 4 opens by saying that Australian values are central to our community remaining a secure, prosperous and peaceful place to live.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: Why do so many people want to become Australian citizens?
options_en: Citizens are guaranteed a well-paid job by the government.
Citizens no longer have to obey laws they disagree with.
Australia's values, which define and shape the country.
explanation_en: Part 4 says our values define and shape our country and are a reason why so many people want to become Australian citizens.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: A migrant worries that Australian laws protect only people born in Australia. Which is correct?
options_en: Only people born in Australia are protected by the law.
All Australians are protected by the laws and legal system.
Only people who can afford a lawyer are protected by the law.
explanation_en: Part 4's section on the Rule of Law says all Australians are protected by our laws and legal systems, which maintain a peaceful and orderly society.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: To 'respect' a person means to
options_en: show consideration for them, and for the decisions they make.
agree with everything they say and believe about every topic.
follow their instructions without ever questioning them or their reasons.
explanation_en: The glossary to the testable section defines respect as showing consideration for someone as a person, or for a decision they have made.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: A local councillor says council members do not need to follow parking rules because of their position. Which reflects Australian values?
options_en: Only elected officials above councillor rank are exempt
Councillors may set aside minor rules while they are on council duty
Everyone is equal before the law; nobody stands above it
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says all Australians are equal in relation to the law and no person or group is above it.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: A tradesperson is offered cash to skip a required safety check because 'no one will ever look'. According to Australian values, he should
options_en: do the check only if the customer insists
take the cash, since no inspector will ever find out
follow the law even though no one is watching
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says you should follow the law even if no one is watching, and that breaking it brings penalties.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: A visitor says Australian laws do not apply to him because he is only in the country for a short time. Which is correct?
options_en: Australia's laws cover everyone here, whatever their background
Short-term visitors follow only the laws of their own home country
Laws apply to visitors only after six months
explanation_en: The Australian values section says Australian laws apply to all people in Australia regardless of background or culture.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: A man breaks a law and says he should face no penalty because he disagrees with that law. Which statement is correct?
options_en: Disagreement with a law is a legal defence
Penalties apply only to laws a person personally agrees with
He should face the penalty; everyone must obey the law
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says everybody should obey the law and not break it at any time, otherwise they will face penalties.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: A group wants a new law introduced. Under Australia's parliamentary democracy, who decides whether it becomes law?
options_en: A parliament elected by the people
The leaders of the largest religious groups
The judges of the High Court
explanation_en: The parliamentary democracy section says our laws are determined by parliaments elected by the people.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Parliamentary democracy

stem_en: At a dinner, a guest says the Australian government's power comes from the King. Which is correct according to Australian values?
options_en: Power comes from the largest political party
Power comes from the King and is exercised by the Governor-General
Power comes from the Australian people, who elect representatives
explanation_en: The parliamentary democracy section says the power of the government comes from the Australian people because citizens vote for people to represent them.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Parliamentary democracy

stem_en: A friend says ordinary citizens have no part in how Australia is governed. Which is correct?
options_en: Governing is left entirely to public servants
Only members of registered political parties take part in governing
Citizens are involved, because they elect the law-making parliaments
explanation_en: The parliamentary democracy section says Australian citizens are involved in how the country is governed because laws are made by parliaments they elect.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Parliamentary democracy

stem_en: A radio station broadcasts commentary strongly criticising a government minister. In Australia this is
options_en: illegal unless the minister has approved the commentary in advance
allowed only on government-owned stations
allowed, since the media have the same free speech as individuals
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says newspapers, television and radio outlets have the same freedom to say and write what they think, within the law.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: A new arrival wants to criticise a government decision but worries it is illegal to disagree with the government. Which is correct?
options_en: People may share their views on any topic, within the law
Criticism is allowed only during election campaigns
Only Australian-born citizens may criticise the government
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says people in Australia are free to say and write what they think about any topic, so long as it is within the law.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: A protester holds a sign with a lawful message that offends a passer-by, who demands it be taken down. According to Australian values,
options_en: the police must settle who is right
the sign must be taken down as soon as anyone objects to it
the protester's lawful expression should be respected
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says other people's freedom of speech and expression must be respected, as long as the expression is lawful.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: A man's relatives insist he must join their religious organisation. In Australia
options_en: adult family members can be required to join by their relatives
he must join if most of his family belongs
no one can be compelled to join an organisation
explanation_en: The freedom of association section says individuals cannot be compelled to join an organisation or forced to leave it.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of association

stem_en: A cultural group wants to hold a peaceful protest against a company's decision. In Australia this is
options_en: allowed; people may lawfully protest against an organisation
allowed only when the protest targets a government decision
illegal unless the company gives permission
explanation_en: The freedom of association section says Australians can gather freely to protest against a government action or an organisation, provided the protest is lawful and peaceful.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of association

stem_en: A manager tells a worker she must resign from her trade union or be dismissed. According to Australian values this is
options_en: acceptable, because employers decide which memberships staff hold
acceptable if the union is small
not acceptable; people cannot be forced to leave an organisation
explanation_en: The freedom of association section says individuals cannot be compelled to join an organisation or forced to leave it.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of association

stem_en: A couple asks what could happen if they arrange a forced marriage in Australia. Under Australian law,
options_en: they would only receive a warning
it is a private family matter with no legal consequence
it can bring severe penalties, including imprisonment
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says practices such as forced marriage and polygamy are against the law and can result in severe penalties, including imprisonment.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: A café owner wants to pay staff who follow one religion less than the others. In Australia,
options_en: everyone should have equal opportunity regardless of religion
pay can be set according to religion if the staff member agrees
religion may affect pay in family businesses
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says all people should be given equal opportunity to pursue their goals regardless of ethnicity or religion.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: A group puts up flyers saying people of a certain faith should leave the suburb. In Australian society this is
options_en: acceptable as free speech
acceptable if the faith concerned is a minority one in the suburb
not acceptable; religious intolerance has no place in Australia
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says religious intolerance is not acceptable in Australian society.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: A person follows a religion that very few other Australians share. How does the government treat her?
options_en: Equally, whatever her religion or beliefs
With fewer rights than members of larger religions
She must register her religion to be treated equally
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says the government treats all citizens equally, whatever their religion or beliefs.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: A landlord refuses to rent to a couple because of their sexual orientation. In Australia, this
options_en: is allowed if the landlord gives a reason in writing
is allowed, because landlords are free to choose their own tenants
goes against the equal rights Australia values and protects by law
explanation_en: The equality section says Australia values the equal rights of all people regardless of sexual orientation, and laws protect people from being treated differently.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: A woman wants to join the Australian Defence Force. Her brother says only men may serve. Which is correct?
options_en: Women need their family's permission to join
Women may serve only in office roles away from the front line
Men and women can equally join the Defence Force and police
explanation_en: The equality section says both men and women can join the Australian Defence Force and the police force, among other equal rights.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: A husband says his wife is not allowed to take a job outside the home. According to Australian values,
options_en: both men and women have equal access to employment
a wife may work only with her husband's written consent
the husband decides whether his wife works
explanation_en: The equality section says both men and women have equal access to education and employment and make their own choices about personal matters.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: A bank offers lower loan rates to customers from one ethnic background only. In Australia, this
options_en: is how the law is meant to work
is acceptable if the bank is privately owned and discloses the policy
goes against the rule that no background gets preferential treatment
explanation_en: The equality section says the law is applied so that people from different backgrounds are not given preferential treatment, nor discriminated against.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: A partner repeatedly threatens and frightens the other at home, without ever hitting them. In Australia,
options_en: only physical violence is against the law
this is a private family matter that Australian law does not cover
the law protects people from intimidation as well as violence
explanation_en: The equality section says men and women are protected by the law from intimidation or violence, and Part 3 adds that threats aimed at controlling a partner are family violence.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: A 70-year-old is refused a place in a course purely because of his age. In Australia, this
options_en: goes against the equal rights people have regardless of age
is acceptable for popular courses with a limited number of places
is acceptable because age limits are normal
explanation_en: The equality section says Australian society values the equal rights of all people regardless of age, and laws protect people from being treated differently.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: A manager promotes staff who attended the same private school as him rather than those who perform best. Which reflects Australian values?
options_en: Connections from school are a fair basis for deciding promotions
Achievement should come from hard work and talent, not class
Promotion is entirely the manager's private choice
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says people should not be limited by class distinction and that achievement should result from hard work and talents.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: A migrant doubts she could ever lead a business in Australia because she arrived recently. Which statement is correct?
options_en: Leadership roles are reserved for people who were born in Australia
Many new migrants have become leaders in business through hard work
Migrants may lead only businesses in their own community
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says many new migrants have become leaders in business, their profession, the arts, public service and sport through hard work and enterprise.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: A job advertisement says applicants must come from a particular ethnic background. In Australia,
options_en: jobs should be based on skills and experience, not ethnicity
employers may choose staff by ethnicity to suit their customers
ethnicity can be a requirement for jobs in small businesses
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says a person should get a job based on their skills and experience, not because of their gender, wealth or ethnicity.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: Someone says people born into poor families should accept they will never succeed. Which reflects the Australian 'fair go'?
options_en: Success is decided mainly by family wealth
Everyone, whatever their background, gets an equal chance to succeed
Only those with the right family connections can succeed in Australia
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says everyone, regardless of their background, is given an equal opportunity to achieve success in life.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: A club prints a newsletter containing racially offensive jokes about one of its members. In Australia, this
options_en: is acceptable because it is only a club publication
is acceptable as long as the member is not named
is racism, which has no place in Australia
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says racism has no place in Australia, including creating or sharing racially offensive material on the internet or in other publications.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: During a community debate, one participant interrupts and insults everyone who disagrees with him. Which behaviour is expected instead?
options_en: Listening to others and respecting views that differ from your own
Leaving the debate as soon as anyone expresses a different opinion
Only speaking with people who share your views
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says tolerance means listening to others and respecting their views and opinions, even when they are different from your own.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A 19-year-old asks whether the age of sexual consent is the same in every part of Australia. Which is correct?
options_en: It is 18 everywhere in Australia
It is 16 or 17, depending on the state or territory
There is no legal age of consent anywhere in Australia
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says there are strict laws on the age of sexual consent, which is 16 or 17 depending on the state or territory.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A coach tells his players to answer a rival team's taunts with their fists. According to Australian values, this
options_en: is acceptable because sport is competitive
is wrong, because violence of any kind is illegal in Australia
is acceptable if the other team's players started the taunting
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says violence of any kind is illegal and that Australians believe in peaceful disagreement.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A neighbour from a different culture makes lawful lifestyle choices you find strange. You should
options_en: report the neighbour's unusual choices to the local council
respect the neighbour's freedom, dignity and choices
try to make the neighbour change
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says individuals must respect the freedom and dignity of others, and their opinions and choices.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A woman is told she must put up with threats and intimidation from her partner because 'that is marriage'. Which is correct?
options_en: Everyone has the right to be safe from violence and intimidation
Threats made within a marriage are a private matter for the couple
Only physical harm counts under Australian law
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says Australians believe above all in the right to be safe and free from violence and intimidation, and that abuse of any kind is illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: A new citizen says Australian values only matter on the day of the ceremony. Which statement is correct?
options_en: Values apply only to people who hold elected public office in Australia
Citizenship means living these values daily, at home and locally
Values matter only during elections
explanation_en: The Australian values section says citizenship is about living out the values in your everyday life and in your local community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: A small-business owner says workplace safety laws are optional for businesses as small as his. In Australia,
options_en: small businesses may choose which of the workplace laws they follow
everyone must obey the law at all times, whatever the business size
laws apply only to businesses with employees
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says everybody should obey the law and not break it at any time, otherwise they will face penalties.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: Which of these is one of the things Australian values are based on?
options_en: Wealth
Fairness
Tradition
explanation_en: The Australian values section says the values are based on freedom, respect, fairness and equality of opportunity.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: Which of these is against the law in Australia?
options_en: Divorce
Marriage between two men
Polygamy
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says polygamy and forced marriage are against the law, while the equality section says divorce and same-sex marriage are lawful.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: Which behaviour shows commitment to the Rule of Law?
options_en: Following a law even when no one is watching
Obeying only the laws that you personally agree with
Paying a fine only if you are caught
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says you should follow the law even if no one is watching.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: Which of these describes parliamentary democracy in Australia?
options_en: Laws decided by the leaders of the largest religious groups
Laws determined by parliaments elected by the people
Laws made by the King alone
explanation_en: The parliamentary democracy section says our laws are determined by parliaments elected by the people.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Parliamentary democracy

stem_en: Which of these is protected as freedom of speech in Australia?
options_en: Promoting violence against a group
Making false allegations about another person online
Peacefully protesting against a government action
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section allows peaceful protest but says promoting violence and making false allegations are against Australian values and law.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: Joining a trade union, joining a choir or leaving a sports club are all examples of which Australian value?
options_en: Parliamentary democracy
Freedom of association
Commitment to the Rule of Law
explanation_en: The freedom of association section says people are free to join or leave any group voluntarily and cannot be compelled to join or forced to leave.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of association

stem_en: Which statement about religion reflects Australian values?
options_en: Religious rules carry no legal force in Australia
Religious law overrides Australian law for believers
Everyone must follow the national religion
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says religious laws have no legal status and Australian law must be followed by everyone, even where it differs from religious laws.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: Which of these shows equality of all people under the law?
options_en: Preferential treatment for one faith
A man's evidence counting for more than a woman's in court
A Buddhist and a Christian receiving the same treatment
explanation_en: The equality section gives the example that Buddhists and people of all other faiths receive the same treatment as Christians.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: Which of these is a right that both men and women have in Australia?
options_en: Deciding a spouse's religion
Standing for parliament
Preventing a spouse from working
explanation_en: The equality section says both men and women can vote, stand for parliament, join the Defence Force and the police, and make their own personal choices.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: Which of these shows the 'fair go' in a workplace?
options_en: Hiring the applicant with the best skills and experience
Hiring only people who come from wealthy, well-connected families
Hiring according to ethnic background
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says the law supports selecting the person with the best skills and experience when an organisation fills a job.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: Which of these behaviours has no place in Australia?
options_en: Peaceful disagreement
Volunteering
Racism
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says racism has no place in Australia.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Which of these is a form of violence that is illegal in Australia?
options_en: Verbal abuse
Peaceful disagreement
Lawful protest
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says violence of any kind, including verbal and physical abuse, is illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Which of these is a criminal offence in Australia?
options_en: Applying to a court for a divorce without the spouse's consent
Physical violence against a spouse or partner
Marrying someone of the same sex
explanation_en: The equality section says physical violence against a spouse or partner is never acceptable and is a criminal offence, while divorce and same-sex marriage are lawful.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: One of these is against Australian law. Which one?
options_en: Changing from one religion to another
Choosing to follow no religion
Forcing someone into a marriage
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says forced marriage is against the law, while people are free to follow any religion they choose, or none.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: Which of these is illegal in Australia, even though freedom of speech is valued?
options_en: Encouraging others to break the law
Criticising the government in a newspaper article
Protesting peacefully
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says it is illegal to make false allegations or encourage others to break the law, while lawful criticism and peaceful protest are allowed.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: Which of these is an Australian value?
options_en: Loyalty to one political party
Equality of opportunity
Following a single religion
explanation_en: The Australian values section lists equality of opportunity among the values on which Australian values are based.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: Which Australian value holds that nobody, and no group, stands above the law?
options_en: Freedom of association
Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'
Commitment to the Rule of Law
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says all Australians are equal in relation to the law and no person or group is above the law.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: A worker gets a job because of her skills, not her wealth. Which Australian value does this show?
options_en: Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'
Freedom of speech and freedom of expression
Parliamentary democracy
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says a person should get a job based on skills and experience, not because of gender, wealth or ethnicity.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: People who disagree peacefully and respect each other's opinions are showing which Australian value?
options_en: Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'
Mutual respect and tolerance for others
Freedom of religion
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says Australians believe in peaceful disagreement and in respecting others' views and opinions.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Which of these are people in Australia free to do under freedom of religion?
options_en: Follow no religion at all
Break a law their religion permits
Require others to follow their religion
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says people are free to follow any religion they choose, but religious practices must not break Australian laws.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: What do Australian values do for the country?
options_en: They replace the need for written laws
They define and shape the country
They apply only to new citizens
explanation_en: The Australian values section says our values define and shape our country and are a reason so many people want to become citizens.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: Under the Rule of Law, what protects all Australians?
options_en: Our laws and legal systems
Membership of a political party
The Governor-General's reserve powers
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says all Australians are protected by our laws and legal systems.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: As part of mutual respect, what do Australians believe in 'above all'?
options_en: The right to be safe and free from violence and intimidation
The right to own as much property as they wish anywhere in Australia
The right to a free education
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says Australians believe in peaceful disagreement and above all the right to be safe and free from violence and intimidation.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: As part of freedom of speech, what must be respected as long as it is lawful?
options_en: Every decision made by the government
Other people's freedom of speech and expression
All religious rules and customs
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says other people's freedom of speech and freedom of expression must be respected, as long as such expression is lawful.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: What is true about leaving a group in Australia?
options_en: Leaving requires the group's permission
People may leave a group only after at least a year of membership
People are free to leave any group voluntarily, within the law
explanation_en: The freedom of association section says people are free to join or leave any group voluntarily as long as it is within the law.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of association

stem_en: What penalty can polygamy or forced marriage bring in Australia?
options_en: A small fine only
Severe penalties, including imprisonment
Loss of the right to vote in federal elections
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says polygamy and forced marriage are against the law and can result in severe legal penalties, including imprisonment.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: Regardless of ethnicity or religion, what should all people in Australia be given?
options_en: An equal chance to pursue their goals and interests
A government position
Exemption from any laws that conflict with their faith
explanation_en: The freedom of religion section says all people should be given equal opportunity to pursue their goals and interests regardless of ethnicity or religion, within the law.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of religion

stem_en: Under Australian law, who may apply to the courts for a divorce?
options_en: Only the husband
Either the husband or the wife
Only both spouses, applying together
explanation_en: The equality section says either a husband or a wife may apply for a divorce, even if the other spouse wishes to continue the marriage.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: In which fields have many new migrants become leaders in Australia?
options_en: Business, the professions, the arts, public service and sport
Only within their own ethnic communities and places of worship
Only in farming and mining
explanation_en: The 'fair go' section says many new migrants have become leaders in business, their profession, the arts, public service and sport.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of opportunity and a 'fair go'

stem_en: Violence of any kind is illegal in Australia. Which two kinds of abuse does this include?
options_en: Financial and emotional
Verbal and physical
Online and written
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says violence of any kind, including verbal and physical abuse, is illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Besides the internet, where is making racially abusive comments unacceptable?
options_en: Only inside private homes with the doors closed
In a public place or at a sporting event
Only in parliament
explanation_en: The mutual respect section says racism includes making racially abusive comments in a public place or at a sporting event.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: How are Buddhists and people of other faiths treated in Australia compared with Christians?
options_en: They receive the same treatment
They have fewer legal rights than Christians
They pay higher taxes
explanation_en: The equality section gives the example that Buddhists and people of all other faiths receive the same treatment as Christians.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: Under the Rule of Law, everybody in Australia should obey the law
options_en: unless they hold public office
every time, with no exceptions for anyone
only when the police are present to see them
explanation_en: The Rule of Law section says everybody should obey the law and not break it at any time, otherwise they will face penalties.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Commitment to the Rule of Law

stem_en: In Australia, newspapers, television and radio outlets
options_en: have the same freedom of speech as individuals
must have their stories approved by the government
may only report official government statements
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says newspapers, television and radio outlets have the same freedom as individuals to say and write what they think.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: In Australia, men and women alike are entitled to decide for themselves about
options_en: which laws they will obey
whether or not they will pay tax on their earnings
personal matters such as marriage and religion
explanation_en: The equality section says both men and women have the right to make their own independent choices about personal matters such as marriage and religion.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Equality of all people under the law

stem_en: In Australia, tolerance of peaceful public protest is
options_en: a threat to public order
an essential part of democracy
allowed only with government permission
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says Australians may peacefully protest against government actions because tolerance of peaceful public protest is an essential part of democracy.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: Australian values are based on four things. Which of these is NOT one of them?
options_en: Freedom
Respect
Wealth
explanation_en: The Australian values section names freedom, respect, fairness and equality of opportunity as the basis of Australian values.
guideRef: Part 4 — Australian values

stem_en: Freedom of speech in Australia does NOT cover which of these?
options_en: Promoting violence against a group of people
Criticising the government's decisions in a newspaper
Protesting peacefully
explanation_en: The freedom of speech section says it is never acceptable to promote violence against another person or group, while criticism and peaceful protest are allowed.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of speech

stem_en: Which of these is NOT something people in Australia may freely do?
options_en: Join a political party of their own choosing
Force someone to join a religious group
Leave a trade union
explanation_en: The freedom of association section says people may freely join or leave any legal organisation but cannot compel anyone to join or stay.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Freedom of association

stem_en: Which of these is NOT an example of racism?
options_en: Sharing racially offensive material online
Cheering for a sports team from another country
Making racially abusive comments at a sporting event
explanation_en: The mutual respect section gives racially offensive online material and racially abusive comments in public or at sporting events as examples of racism.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our values — Mutual respect and tolerance for others

stem_en: Australians expect everyone living in Australia to
options_en: stay out of community life until they become citizens.
take part in society and contribute to the community.
contribute only if they were born in Australia.
explanation_en: The booklet's section on making a contribution says Australians expect everyone living in Australia to participate in society and contribute to the community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: In Australia, everyone has a responsibility to
options_en: try to support themselves and their family.
rely on the government for all of their needs.
support only themselves and no one else.
explanation_en: Part 4 says everyone has a responsibility to try and support themselves and their families when they are able to do so.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: An elderly neighbour is unwell and cannot cook, so you take her a hot meal. Which Australian value does this show?
options_en: Mateship.
Loyalty to the government.
Parliamentary democracy.
explanation_en: The booklet gives taking a meal to an elderly neighbour as an example of mateship, which means helping each other in times of need.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: In Australia, 'mateship' means
options_en: helping only your close friends.
helping others only in return for payment.
helping each other in times of need.
explanation_en: Part 4 says Australians value mateship: we help each other in times of need, for example by driving a friend to a medical appointment.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: Which of these is a benefit of volunteering?
options_en: Earning a high salary without any training or experience.
Being excused from paying tax.
Learning new skills and a stronger sense of belonging.
explanation_en: The booklet says volunteering is an opportunity to share knowledge, learn new skills, and increase your integration into and sense of belonging to the community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: A volunteer is a person who
options_en: is paid by the council to help the community.
is ordered by a court to do community work.
gives their time without expecting payment.
explanation_en: The glossary defines a volunteer as a person who gives their time to a person or organisation without expecting payment.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: Which language does Australian society value as the national language and a unifying element?
options_en: English.
Latin.
The language of the largest migrant group.
explanation_en: Part 4 says Australian society values the English language as the national language and an important unifying element of society.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: A new migrant asks why she should make an effort to learn English. Which answer is correct?
options_en: The law requires everyone in Australia to speak only English at home.
It helps with education, work and fitting into the community.
Only fluent English speakers are allowed to vote.
explanation_en: The booklet says learning English helps people get an education and a job and better integrate into the community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: Applicants for Australian citizenship whose native language is not English must
options_en: already speak and write English fluently before they apply.
promise to stop speaking their own language.
undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn English.
explanation_en: Part 4 says applicants for citizenship must undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn the English language if it is not their native language.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: You suspect your neighbour is planning to commit a serious crime. What should you do?
options_en: Tell Australian government authorities about it as soon as you can.
Wait until the crime has been committed, then report it.
Confront the neighbour on your own and say nothing to anyone in authority.
explanation_en: The booklet says that if people suspect a friend or neighbour may be planning a serious crime, they should report it to Australian government authorities as soon as possible.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: You know that a child is being abused. What should you do?
options_en: Keep quiet, because it is a private family matter.
Report it to the police so they can investigate.
Wait and hope that someone else reports it.
explanation_en: Part 4 says that if a person sees or knows of a child being abused, they should report it to the police to investigate.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: Which of these is an example of cyber abuse?
options_en: Sharing sexual photos of someone online without their consent.
Posting a photo of your dinner online for all your friends to see.
Sending a work email to a colleague about a meeting.
explanation_en: The booklet lists sharing sexual photos or videos online without consent, online stalking and racially abusive comments online as examples of cyber abuse.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: A man keeps tracking and messaging a woman online after she has asked him to stop. In Australia this is
options_en: online stalking, which is cyber abuse and not accepted.
acceptable, because it only happens online.
acceptable as long as he never tries to meet her in person.
explanation_en: Part 4 says online abuse, or cyber abuse, is not accepted in Australia and gives stalking a person online as an example; many forms are illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: In the citizenship pledge, new citizens pledge their loyalty to
options_en: the Prime Minister.
Australia and its people.
their own state or territory.
explanation_en: The booklet says that in the citizenship pledge, Australian citizens pledge their loyalty to Australia and its people.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: Can an Australian citizen also be a citizen of another country?
options_en: No, never.
Yes, if that country's laws allow it.
Only if they were born outside Australia.
explanation_en: Part 4 says Australian citizens may also hold the citizenship of another country if the laws of that country allow; this is dual or multiple citizenship.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: A dual citizen living in Australia says he only has to follow the laws of his other country. Which is correct?
options_en: He must follow all Australian laws while in Australia.
He is right; dual citizens choose which country's laws apply.
He must follow Australian laws only on weekdays.
explanation_en: The booklet says that even if a person is also a citizen of another country, an Australian citizen within Australia must follow all Australian laws at all times.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: Some Australian laws apply to Australians even when they are overseas. Which is an example?
options_en: Australians must drive on the left when overseas.
Sexual activity with a child under 16 is illegal here or overseas.
Australians must vote in the elections of any other country they visit.
explanation_en: Part 4 says some Australian laws must be followed overseas, for example it is illegal for Australians to be involved in sexual activity with a child under 16, here or overseas.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: A public servant posts official government secrets on social media. This
options_en: is acceptable as freedom of speech.
is fine if only a few people ever see the post.
undermines Australia's interests and security.
explanation_en: The booklet says using social media to share official government secrets would be undermining Australia's interests.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: Someone spreads messages designed to make people fear a particular ethnic community. This
options_en: is acceptable if the messages are sincere.
is acceptable as long as it is online.
damages Australian community relations.
explanation_en: Part 4 says promoting distrust in and fear of an ethnic community would damage Australian community relations.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: In Australian society, 'integration' means
options_en: migrants giving up every part of the culture they grew up with.
migrants adapting so they can take part in their new society.
the moment a migrant becomes an Australian citizen.
explanation_en: The glossary defines integration as the process of adaptation by migrants so they can participate in and contribute to their new, evolving society.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: A new citizen says that now he has his certificate he has no further duties to Australia. What does Australian citizenship actually mean?
options_en: Being ready to carry out your responsibilities as a citizen
That your responsibilities to the Australian community have ended
That only voting remains as a duty
explanation_en: The 'making a contribution' section says citizenship means you are ready to fulfil your responsibilities as an Australian citizen.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: A healthy adult who could work says the government should support him instead. In Australia,
options_en: only people born overseas must support themselves
support is a right that replaces any need to look for paid work
everyone should try to support themselves and family when able
explanation_en: The 'making a contribution' section says everyone has a responsibility to try and support themselves and their families when they are able to do so.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: Your friend has no way to get to a medical appointment. Which action reflects the Australian idea of mateship?
options_en: Suggesting she cancel it
Telling her to call a taxi instead
Driving her to the appointment
explanation_en: The compassion section gives driving a friend to a medical appointment as an example of mateship, helping each other in times of need.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: A new migrant feels isolated and wants to feel he belongs in his community. What helps with this?
options_en: Volunteering, which builds integration and belonging
Waiting until he becomes a citizen
Keeping only to people from his own country of origin
explanation_en: The compassion section says volunteering helps people share knowledge, learn skills and increase their integration into and sense of belonging to the community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: A retiree with spare time asks how he can help strengthen his local community. Which answer is correct?
options_en: Communities are strengthened only by programs the government funds
Only paid work strengthens a community
Join Australia's tradition of community service and volunteering
explanation_en: The compassion section says Australia has a strong tradition of community service and volunteering to look out for each other and strengthen the community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: A migrant says she does not need to learn English because her neighbours speak her language. What is expected of people living in Australia?
options_en: Learning English is optional if a community shares another language
English is needed only for citizenship paperwork
Everyone living here should try to learn English
explanation_en: The English language section says people living in Australia should make an effort to learn English, which is a unifying element of society.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: A citizenship applicant speaks little English and asks what is expected of her. As an applicant, she must
options_en: promise to speak only English at home
pass a university-level English examination before applying
undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn English
explanation_en: The English language section says applicants whose native language is not English must undertake to make reasonable efforts to learn it.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: Someone shares sexual photos of a former partner online without consent. In Australia, this is
options_en: a private matter between the two people
acceptable once the relationship between them has ended
cyber abuse, which is not accepted and is often illegal
explanation_en: The 'keeping our society safe' section gives sharing sexual photos or videos online without consent as an example of cyber abuse, much of which is illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: A student posts racially abusive comments about a classmate on social media. This is
options_en: cyber abuse, which is not accepted in Australia
acceptable if the comments are only meant as a joke
a matter for the school only
explanation_en: The 'keeping our society safe' section lists racially abusive comments about a person online among the forms of cyber abuse that are not accepted.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: An Australian citizen travelling abroad assumes no Australian law can apply to him outside the country. Which is correct?
options_en: Australian laws apply overseas only to people with dual citizenship
No Australian law applies once you leave Australia
Some Australian laws must be followed by citizens even overseas
explanation_en: The loyalty section says some Australian laws must be followed by Australian citizens even when they are overseas, such as the law against sexual activity with a child under 16.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: A woman becoming an Australian citizen wants to keep the citizenship of her birth country. Under Australian law, she
options_en: may keep it if the laws of that country allow it
may keep it only for five years
must give up her other citizenship at the ceremony
explanation_en: The loyalty section says Australian citizens may also hold the citizenship of another country if the laws of that country allow, known as dual or multiple citizenship.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: A person is asked to hand official government secrets to a foreign group. Doing so would
options_en: be acceptable as long as no money changes hands
undermine Australia's interests and security
be a matter of personal choice
explanation_en: The loyalty section says Australian society is based on shared obligations not to undermine Australia's interests and security, giving sharing official secrets as an example.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: After a flood, local community groups collect food and clothing for affected families. Which Australian tradition does this show?
options_en: Coming together in a crisis to take care of each other
Leaving disaster relief entirely to government agencies
Helping only members of your own community
explanation_en: The loyalty section says Australians come together in times of crisis, as many multicultural communities did during the 2019-20 bushfires.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: A man says he need not do anything for his community because he already pays tax. What is expected in Australia?
options_en: Paying tax is the only contribution anyone ever needs to make
Everyone living in Australia should take part and contribute
Only citizens, not residents, are expected to contribute
explanation_en: The 'making a contribution' section says Australians expect everyone living in Australia to participate in our society and make a contribution to our community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: A frail elderly man who lives alone next door has not been seen for several days. Which response reflects mateship?
options_en: Visiting to check that he is well
Waiting for his family to notice
Assuming it is none of your business
explanation_en: The compassion section gives visiting someone who is sick, frail or lonely as an example of mateship.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: At the citizenship ceremony a new citizen wonders what the pledge commits him to. He pledges
options_en: loyalty to a political party
loyalty to Australia and its people
loyalty to his state or territory government
explanation_en: The loyalty section says that in the citizenship pledge, Australian citizens pledge their loyalty to Australia and its people.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: A friend says cyber abuse is not a real crime in Australia. Which is correct?
options_en: Online behaviour is never covered by Australian law
Much cyber abuse is against the law in Australia
Cyber abuse is illegal only if it happens at work
explanation_en: The 'keeping our society safe' section says online abuse is not accepted in Australia and that many forms of cyber abuse are illegal.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: A man born overseas says he can never truly be part of Australia's story. Which statement is correct?
options_en: Only people who were born in Australia can be part of the nation's story
As a citizen he joins the nation's story and helps shape its future
New citizens join the story only after ten years
explanation_en: The 'in conclusion' section says that as an Australian citizen you become part of our nation's story and will contribute to our future.
guideRef: Part 4 — In conclusion

stem_en: Which of these is an example of mateship?
options_en: Paying someone to mow your lawn each week
Taking a meal to an elderly neighbour
Lending money at interest
explanation_en: The compassion section gives taking a meal to an elderly neighbour as an example of mateship.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: Which of these online actions is unacceptable in Australia?
options_en: Posting photos of your own holiday
Commenting on the weather forecast
Stalking a person online
explanation_en: The 'keeping our society safe' section lists stalking a person online among the forms of cyber abuse that are not accepted in Australia.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: Which of these should be reported to Australian authorities as soon as possible?
options_en: A friend who is planning a serious crime
A neighbour's loud party that runs late into the night
A colleague's late tax return
explanation_en: The 'keeping our society safe' section says people who suspect a friend or neighbour is planning a serious crime should report it to authorities as soon as possible.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: Which of these would undermine Australia's interests and security?
options_en: Volunteering at a food bank
Sharing official government secrets on social media
Learning English at evening classes at the local library
explanation_en: The loyalty section gives using social media to share official government secrets as an example of undermining Australia's interests.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: Which of these can volunteering give you?
options_en: Learning new skills
Earning a high income
Avoiding tax
explanation_en: The compassion section says volunteering is an opportunity to share knowledge, learn new skills and increase integration into the community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Compassion for those in need

stem_en: Which statement about English in Australia is correct?
options_en: Other languages are banned in public
It is the only language permitted in Australian workplaces and schools
It is vital for economic participation and social cohesion
explanation_en: The English language section says English is essential for economic participation and social cohesion and an important unifying element of society.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: Which of these is a responsibility everyone in Australia has?
options_en: Owning a home
Trying to support themselves and their family when able
Joining a political party before every federal election is held
explanation_en: The 'making a contribution' section says everyone has a responsibility to try and support themselves and their families when they are able to.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: Which of these reflects loyalty to Australia?
options_en: Following Australian laws at all times, even as a dual citizen
Sharing official government secrets with friends on social media
Promoting fear of an ethnic community
explanation_en: The loyalty section says even a dual citizen must follow all Australian laws at all times, and warns against undermining Australia's interests or community relations.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: What does Australian citizenship give you the opportunity to do?
options_en: Avoid paying some taxes
Fully participate in the nation's life and community
Choose which Australian laws to follow and which to ignore
explanation_en: The 'making a contribution' section says citizenship gives you the opportunity to fully participate in our nation's life and community.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Making a contribution

stem_en: During the 2019-20 bushfires, what did members of the Sikh community donate to communities and firefighters in Queensland?
options_en: Thousands of bottles of water
Fire trucks
Temporary housing for families
explanation_en: The loyalty section recounts that members of the Sikh community donated thousands of bottles of water to communities and firefighters in Queensland during the bushfires.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: How is Australian citizenship best described?
options_en: As a legal formality
As our common bond
As a reward for paying tax
explanation_en: The 'in conclusion' section ends by saying Australia welcomes you and that citizenship is our common bond.
guideRef: Part 4 — In conclusion

stem_en: What is 'cyber abuse'?
options_en: Any use of a computer or mobile phone for work or study purposes
Using technology to threaten, harass or humiliate a person
Sharing news articles online
explanation_en: The glossary defines cyber abuse as behaviour that uses technology to threaten, intimidate, harass or humiliate someone with the intent to hurt them.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: Which phrase from the citizenship pledge means 'from now and in the future'?
options_en: Citizenship is our common bond
Fair go
From this time forward
explanation_en: The glossary explains the pledge's words 'from this time forward' as meaning from now and in the future.
guideRef: Glossary of testable section

stem_en: Besides being the national language, what role does English play in Australian society?
options_en: An important unifying element
A requirement for permanent residence
The only language spoken in homes
explanation_en: The English language section says Australian society values English as the national language and an important unifying element of society.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — English as the national language

stem_en: In times of crisis, Australians
options_en: wait for help to arrive from the government alone
look after only their own families
come together and take care of each other
explanation_en: The loyalty section says that in Australia we come together in times of crisis and take care of each other in good times and bad.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia

stem_en: Which of these is NOT an example of cyber abuse?
options_en: Sending a friend a birthday message
Stalking a person online
Sharing sexual photos online without consent
explanation_en: The 'keeping our society safe' section lists sharing intimate images without consent, online stalking and racially abusive comments as cyber abuse.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Helping to keep our society safe

stem_en: Which of these is NOT true about dual citizenship in Australia?
options_en: An Australian citizen may hold another citizenship if that country allows it
A dual citizen in Australia may choose which country's laws to follow
Dual citizens in Australia must obey every Australian law at all times
explanation_en: The loyalty section says dual citizenship is allowed where the other country permits it, but a dual citizen within Australia must follow all Australian laws at all times.
guideRef: Part 4 — Our community — Loyalty to Australia
